note: The promoted 4-bit/group-64 proposal head is preserved tensor-for-tensor, with the same six bare BF16 precision-island tensors (precision_islands.{q,k,v}.{weight,indices}) in the identical layout and the same total island-row budget (3,072 rows) as the promoted islands artifact; this file is 328 bytes smaller. The only change is which rows are carried exact, chosen by measured contribution to the head's fp32 OUTPUT error: all 1,024 V rows (dropping V collapses the benefit), 128 K rows (K islands are nearly worthless: K1024→K128 at fixed rows costs 0.0 pp; 128 is the smallest count that keeps all six island tensors present as the loader requires), and 1,920 q_proj rows restricted to the sigmoid output-GATE half of each head (row r is a gate row iff r % 512 >= 256): gate error passes a sigmoid and then multiplies the attention output into o_proj and the residual stream with nothing to normalise it away, whereas query error passes q_norm and a shift-invariant softmax and is suppressed. Measured on the fp32 head forward against the pinned bf16 head, this removes 13.55% of head output error vs 12.71% for the promoted selection at the same bytes. Candidate code is unchanged. The head only proposes; the pinned target re-verifies every emitted token. sha256 is the tree digest over the single fetched model.safetensors per the documented rule; bytes is the fetched file size.
